TEXT_D:
Change that Works for You — Building a Fairer Britain (Liberal Democrat Manifesto 2010)

Core purpose: hard‑wire fairness into national life by redistributing power — economic, social, political and financial — away from vested interests and towards citizens. After decades of red–blue, blue–red governments, the Liberal Democrats offer fundamental reform built around four priorities:

1) Fair taxes that put money back in your pocket
- Raise the personal allowance to £10,000, a £700 tax cut for most workers; 3.6m low earners and pensioners lifted out of income tax.
- Paid for by: taxing capital gains at income rates; restricting pension tax relief to the basic rate; a 1% Mansion Tax on property value above £2m; replacing Air Passenger Duty with a fairer per‑plane duty (higher for non‑lifeline domestic flights); robust anti‑avoidance and anti‑evasion action; reform of non‑dom status.
- Credible deficit reduction: over £15bn identified savings (e.g., scrap ID cards/biometric passports/ContactPoint; banking levy; cap public‑sector pay rises at £400 for two years; prison reform; reduce quangos; cancel Eurofighter Tranche 3B). No like‑for‑like Trident replacement; Council on Financial Stability to guide the pace of cuts.

2) A fair chance for every child
- £2.5bn Pupil Premium to cut class sizes and fund one‑to‑one tuition for disadvantaged pupils; earlier SEN assessment and better teacher training.
- Free schools to innovate: an Education Freedom Act; independent Educational Standards Authority; a slimmer core curriculum; reform league tables.
- Transform 14–19 pathways: a General Diploma to combine academic and vocational learning; FE parity; right to study at college from 14.
- Scrap unfair university tuition fees, phased over six years (final‑year fees ended immediately); targeted national bursaries.

3) A fair future: jobs and green growth
- Break up the banks, separate retail from investment, reform bonuses, and create Local Enterprise Funds and Regional Stock Exchanges.
- A UK Infrastructure Bank to crowd in private finance for clean energy and transport.
- One‑year green stimulus to create 100,000 jobs: refurbish shipyards for offshore wind; £400 Eco Cash‑Back; insulate public buildings; bring 250,000 empty homes into use; bus scrappage; major youth work‑experience offer.
- Climate leadership: zero‑carbon Britain by 2050; 40% clean electricity by 2020 (prioritising marine/offshore); home insulation up to £10,000 per home; no new coal without top‑tier CCS; reject new nuclear in favour of cheaper conservation/renewables; build a European Supergrid.
- Transport fairness: shift funding from roads to rail; cut regulated rail fares 1% below inflation annually; regulate buses locally; cancel Heathrow R3; per‑plane duty; plan for fair, revenue‑neutral road pricing later.

4) A fair deal by cleaning up politics and restoring liberties
- End safe seats with fair votes (STV) and cut 150 MPs; fixed‑term parliaments; a fully elected, smaller second chamber; a written constitution via a citizens’ convention.
- Cleaner politics: recall corrupt MPs; cap donations at £10,000; statutory lobbyist register; all candidates and parliamentarians tax‑resident in the UK.
- Freedom Bill: roll back the surveillance state; regulate CCTV; protect trial by jury and free speech; end blanket retention of innocent people’s DNA; scrap ID cards; stop unfair US extraditions.

Public services and communities built on fairness
- NHS: cut waste, not care; protect frontline (cancer, mental health, maternity, dementia); integrate health and social care; prevention first; patient entitlements over targets; elected Local Health Boards; GP choice and email access.
- Families: shared parental leave; flexible working for all; end child detention in immigration; stronger youth services; equal minimum wage from 16; carers’ respite.
- Older people: restore the earnings link (triple lock: earnings, prices or 2.5%); scrap compulsory retirement ages; long‑term plan for a Citizen’s Pension.
- Crime: 3,000 more police funded by scrapping ID cards; empower elected police authorities; target what works, including restorative justice; presumption against short prison sentences; evidence‑based drugs policy.
- Immigration: firm and fair — reinstate exit checks; National Border Force; regional points system; enforce against rogue employers; earned citizenship for long‑settled families pre‑2010; humane, independent asylum system with right to work.
- Pro‑Europe, internationalist and principled abroad: lead EU climate ambition and financial reform; aid at 0.7% of GNI by 2013; defence review; fair pay/housing for forces; no like‑for‑like Trident; uphold human rights, end complicity in torture; two‑state solution and end Gaza blockade.

If you want real, lasting change that works for you, choose fairness: choose the Liberal Democrats.

TEXT_G:
UKIP Manifesto 2010 – Summary (ideological framing retained)

Core mission
- Leave the EU to restore three freedoms: action (sovereign decision-making), resources (keep UK money and cut EU red tape), and people (end rule by unelected EU bodies). Replace the LibLabCon consensus with direct democracy, binding referenda, and real local control.

Economy and tax
- Turbocharge enterprise by simplifying tax: raise the personal allowance to £11,500, merge income tax and Employees’ NI into a single 31% flat rate, and phase out Employers’ NI over five years. Abolish Inheritance Tax when conditions allow.
- Cut the state back to its 1997 size, scrap quangos, and replace VAT with a Local Sales Tax that funds councils; return 50% of business rates to local authorities.
- Repeal up to 120,000 EU rules stifling business; defend the City from harmful EU directives; repatriate financial regulation.
- Restore Bank of England authority, raise bank capital ratios, split retail and investment banking (Glass-Steagall style), and reinstate a “corset” on excessive lending.

Jobs, industry, and skills
- Create one million skilled jobs via long-term national programmes: defence, nuclear power, flood/coastal defences, transport, and prison building—anchoring UK manufacturing.
- Production Enterprise Centres to help SMEs innovate and export.
- Denationalise universities/FE via universal Student/Training Vouchers; scrap EU carbon caps and protect strategic UK firms from predatory takeovers.

Immigration and asylum
- Immediate five-year freeze on permanent immigration; thereafter cap at around 50,000 per year. Leave the EU to regain border control; use time-limited work permits and visas; criminalise overstaying; triple border staff; record all entry/exit.
- No amnesty for illegal immigrants; enforce removals. Reinstate the Primary Purpose Rule; end official multiculturalism; require loyalty undertakings for residents; replace the Human Rights Act and leave the ECHR; tighten asylum with secure centres and first-safe-country rules.

Law, order, and defence
- Victims first: elected Police Boards; “life means life”; double prison places; three-strikes policy; stronger homeowner rights; withdraw from the European Arrest Warrant; youth “boot camps.”
- Increase defence spending by 40%; expand the Army and TA; restore the Navy (including three carriers); strengthen the RAF; back NATO, not EU missions; maintain and renew Trident; cut MoD bureaucracy; improve forces’ pay and care.

Public services
- NHS: no frontline cuts; elected County Health Boards; scrap wasteful tiers; franchise services on fixed budgets; Health Credit Vouchers to enable opting out; restore matrons; free eye tests and dental checks.
- Schools: universal School Vouchers; restore rigour in the three Rs; retain/expand grammar and professional schools; end social engineering; more on-the-job teacher training; elected Education Boards; allow meaningful discipline; support special schools and home education.
- Welfare: replace 70+ benefits with a flat-rate Basic Cash Benefit; allow work up to the personal allowance without penalty; enhance Child Benefit (first three children) and introduce Nursery Vouchers; limit benefits to citizens/residents of 5+ years; “Workfare” for claimants.
- Pensions: non-means-tested £130/week Citizen’s Pension at 65; retarget tax relief; reinstate dividend tax credit; freeze unaffordable public sector schemes; scrap PPF/NEST; avoid an EU pensions trap.

Trade, energy, and environment
- Leave the political EU; pursue a Swiss-style trade deal; reclaim the UK’s WTO seat; lead a Commonwealth Free Trade Area; seek deals with NAFTA/ASEAN; promote real human rights.
- Climate realism: repeal the Climate Change Act; expand nuclear to 50% of electricity; use indigenous coal; oppose uneconomic wind (keep large schemes offshore, market-funded); exit EU carbon schemes; convene a Royal Commission on climate science; fund practical environmental improvements and flood defences; electrify transport.

Infrastructure, housing, constitution, culture
- Transport: invest £3bn/year; build high-speed rail lines; reopen railways; improve roads; fair fuel duty; “Britdisc” for foreign HGVs; oppose Heathrow expansion; build a Thames Estuary hub.
- Housing/planning: tackle demand by controlling immigration; bring empty homes into use; scrap regional quangos/IPC; binding local referenda on major schemes; protect Green Belt via elected Conservators.
- Constitution: Swiss-style initiative and referendum (5% trigger); AV+ voting; elected Police/Health/Education Boards; English-only days at Westminster, with devolved business handled by national MPs; recall powers; abolish regional government; support the monarchy and Church of England.
- Britishness: civic nationalism; oppose multiculturalism/political correctness; protect iconic brands/measures; teach Britain’s contributions; counter extremist Islam (ban burqa/niqab in public buildings, deport radical preachers, reaffirm UK law over sharia); celebrate the Commonwealth; English Parliament; St George’s Day holiday.

Farming, fishing, and community
- Leave the CAP but phase support; promote British produce, ethical labelling, co-ops, and a supermarket ombudsman; review/repeal harmful EU directives.
- Exit the CFP; reclaim a 200nm EEZ; end discards and industrial fishing; rebuild stocks and fleets—returning £2.5bn/year to the UK.
- Protect animal welfare; safeguard Royal Mail/Post Offices; allow designated pub smoking rooms; champion small business.
